placements.why: The document's content — a mandatory signed-manifest gate, its scope across staging and production, and a named owner — names an organizational category for release governance that nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers. placements.title: governing what ships through controlled release gates
placements.frame: What rules, gates, and accountabilities govern the path from build to deploy?

placements.title: a past failure crystallized into a mandatory gate
placements.frame: Does a control here enter as a ratified operational rule justified by a named prior incident, with scope and owner assigned, rather than as a proposal under debate?
placements.why: All four expressions perform the same theme: a signed-manifest gate is stated as a settled operational rule, not a position being argued. src-1 declares the mandate and anchors it in a concrete past incident (two unsigned artifacts reaching staging); src-3 records the gate itself; src-4 fixes its scope across staging and production; src-5 names the accountable owner. The conviction gradient is flat — no hedging, no alternatives — and the justification is incident-driven, making this a thematic subject future envelopes will keep feeding: how past failures get crystallized into ratified deployment controls.
